faqs.q: How much does a Maltese cost to buy?
faqs.a: Reputable breeders typically charge $500–$2,000 for a Maltese puppy. Prices vary by breeder reputation, health testing, and lineage. Rescue adoption fees are typically $100–$500 and include vaccinations, neutering, and microchipping.

faqs.q: What is the monthly cost of owning a Maltese?
faqs.a: Budget $120–$200 per month for a Maltese, covering food, preventive vet care, insurance, grooming and supplies. Small breeds often cost less on food and some products, but vet bills don't proportionally reduce — procedures cost similar amounts regardless of size.

faqs.q: What are the biggest ongoing costs for a Maltese?
faqs.a: The three largest annual expenses are food ($300–600), veterinary care ($400–$1,200 budgeted annually), and pet insurance ($$400–$1,200 per year). Grooming adds $400–$1,200 annually for Malteses due to their coat type.

faqs.q: How much does a Maltese cost in the first year?
faqs.a: Year one costs for a Maltese are significantly higher than subsequent years, typically $1,500–$3,000. This covers the purchase price or adoption fee, initial vet checks, vaccinations, spay/neuter, microchipping, crate, bedding, collar, leads and puppy training classes.

faqs.q: How often should I groom a Maltese?
faqs.a: Malteses need brushing 3–4 times per week to prevent matting.  Nails should be trimmed every 3–4 weeks. Ears should be checked and cleaned monthly.

faqs.q: Do Malteses shed a lot?
faqs.a: Malteses shed minimally. A weekly brush is usually sufficient.

faqs.q: What grooming tools does a Maltese need?
faqs.a: A wide-tooth comb, pin brush, and detangling spray are the core tools for a Maltese's long coat. Add a nail grinder and ear cleaner for complete at-home maintenance.

faqs.q: How often should I bathe a Maltese?
faqs.a: Every 4–6 weeks is appropriate for most Malteses that live indoors. More frequent bathing is needed if they swim or spend time in mud. Over-bathing strips natural skin oils — use a pH-balanced dog shampoo rather than human products.

faqs.q: Are Malteses easy to train?
faqs.a: Malteses are considered easier to train than average — they respond quickly to reward-based methods and generalise cues well. Short 10–15 minute sessions outperform long correction-heavy drills.

faqs.q: What training method works best for a Maltese?
faqs.a: Reward-based training using treats, praise and toy rewards is the most effective and well-researched approach for Malteses. Keep sessions short and positive, end on a success, and vary your rewards to maintain engagement.

faqs.q: At what age should I start training my Maltese?
faqs.a: Start training from the day your puppy arrives home, typically at 8 weeks. The 8–16 week window is the most sensitive socialisation period. Enrol in a puppy class within the first two weeks for structured socialisation alongside basic obedience foundations.

faqs.q: How long does it take to train a Maltese?
faqs.a: Most Malteses learn basic obedience cues (sit, stay, come, down) within 2–4 weeks of daily practice. Reliable recall in distracting environments typically takes 2–3 months of consistent reinforcement.

faqs.q: What health problems do Malteses commonly have?
faqs.a: Malteses are most commonly associated with heart problem and other breed-specific conditions. Regular vet checks, appropriate weight management, and breed-specific screening tests help detect issues early. Ask any breeder for health test results before purchasing.

faqs.q: How long do Malteses live?
faqs.a: Malteses have an average lifespan of 12–15 years. Small breeds often live longer than large breeds. Dental care is particularly important for small dogs, as dental disease is a common longevity issue.

faqs.q: Are Malteses prone to hip dysplasia?
faqs.a: Hip dysplasia is less common in Malteses than in large working breeds, but it can still occur. Responsible breeders screen breeding stock. Keeping your Maltese at a healthy weight is the most effective preventive measure.

faqs.q: What health tests should a Maltese puppy have?
faqs.a: At minimum, your Maltese puppy should have a vet health check, first vaccinations, deworming, and microchipping before coming home. Ask the breeder for parent health certificates relevant to Maltese-specific conditions. A vet check within 72 hours of bringing your puppy home is recommended to establish a baseline.

faqs.q: Are Malteses good with kids?
faqs.a: Malteses are generally known for being friendly and patient, making them well-suited to family life with children. Supervision is always recommended with young children regardless of breed — interactions should be taught from both sides.

faqs.q: Do Malteses get along with other dogs?
faqs.a: Malteses are generally sociable with other dogs, particularly when well-socialised from puppyhood. Introduce new dogs on neutral territory and keep initial meetings brief and positive.

faqs.q: Do Malteses bark a lot?
faqs.a: Malteses are not considered excessive barkers. They may alert to strangers or unusual sounds, but are generally manageable with basic training. Consistent "quiet" reinforcement from puppyhood keeps this in check.

faqs.q: Are Malteses good apartment dogs?
faqs.a: Malteses adapt reasonably well to apartment living, particularly if they receive consistent daily walks and indoor enrichment. Their compact nature makes them less disruptive in confined spaces than high-energy large breeds.

faqs.q: How much exercise does a Maltese need per day?
faqs.a: Malteses need approximately 45–60 minutes of exercise daily. A structured morning walk and an evening sniff walk usually cover their needs. Mental exercise (training sessions, puzzle feeders) counts toward overall stimulation needs and can reduce restless behaviour.

faqs.q: Are Malteses good running partners?
faqs.a: Malteses can join you for moderate runs once fully grown. They're better suited to steady 3–5 mile runs than extended distance. Watch for signs of fatigue and always run in cooler hours during summer.

faqs.q: What happens if a Maltese doesn't get enough exercise?
faqs.a: Malteses are less demanding than high-energy breeds, but chronic under-exercise still leads to weight gain and low-level restlessness. Even lower-energy breeds benefit from a consistent daily walk for both physical health and mental stimulation.

faqs.q: Can a Maltese be off-lead?
faqs.a: Off-lead freedom for a Maltese depends on recall reliability, not breed alone. Train recall from puppyhood using long-line sessions before progressing to full off-lead. A standard 20-foot long-line gives freedom while maintaining safety during the training phase.

faqs.q: How much should I feed my Maltese?
faqs.a: A Maltese needs approximately ½–1½ cups of dry food per day for an adult, split across two meals. Always follow the feeding guide on your specific formula — calorie density varies significantly between brands. Adjust portions based on body condition: you should be able to feel (but not easily see) the ribs.

faqs.q: How many times a day should I feed a Maltese?
faqs.a: Adult Malteses should eat twice daily. Puppies (under 6 months) need 3–4 smaller meals per day to support growth and prevent hypoglycaemia, particularly in small breeds.

faqs.q: What is the best food for a Maltese?
faqs.a: Look for a formula carrying an AAFCO adequacy statement for the correct life stage. A named protein source (chicken, turkey, beef, salmon) should appear first in the ingredient list. Medium-energy Malteses do well on standard adult maintenance formulas with named protein as the first ingredient.

faqs.q: When should I switch my Maltese from puppy to adult food?
faqs.a: Small breeds typically transition to adult food around 12 months. Moving too late keeps them on higher-calorie puppy formulas that can cause weight gain in lower-activity adults.

faqs.q: Is a Maltese a good dog for first-time owners?
faqs.a: Malteses are generally considered suitable for first-time owners. They're responsive to training, manageable in size, and adaptable to different home environments. A puppy class is still recommended to build a strong foundation.

faqs.q: Are Malteses good family dogs?
faqs.a: Malteses are typically affectionate family dogs that do well with children and adapt to household routines. Their sociable nature means they prefer company over isolation.

faqs.q: Do Malteses do well when left alone?
faqs.a: Malteses form strong bonds with their owners and do not do well with extended isolation. Aim for no more than 4–6 hours alone at a time. If your schedule requires longer absences, consider a dog walker, doggy daycare, or a companion dog.

faqs.q: How much time do you need for a Maltese?
faqs.a: Plan for 1.5–2 hours per day dedicated to your Maltese — covering exercise, training, feeding and general interaction. Add 15–30 minutes for grooming 3–4 times weekly. The commitment is consistent year-round, not just when convenient.
